text:
Alex: quick question — we're seeing intermittent 429s + occasional 5xx on streaming completions. What should client libs do for retries and idempotency for streaming vs non-streaming calls?
Priya: short answer: treat streaming differently. full responses (non-streaming) can be retried with idempotency keys; streaming often returns partial data so blind retry can duplicate side effects.
Sam: +1. For non-streaming generation use an Idempotency-Key header and exponential backoff with jitter. Respect Retry-After for 429s when present. Example (node):
```js
// pseudocode
await fetch(url, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': idKey } })
// on 429/5xx -> wait backoff + jitter and retry up to N times
```
Joel: for streaming (server-sent events / chunked) if you can't resume via cursor, best is: 1) surface the partial result to user, 2) write server-side dedupe/compaction, or 3) fall back to a non-streaming single-shot request with idempotency-key.
Alex: ok — what about backoff numbers? exponential base, max, jitter strategy?
Priya: our recommended defaults in SDKs are: initial = 250ms, multiplier = 2, max_backoff = 10s, max_retries = 5. use full-jitter (rand(0, base * 2^n)). For 429 with Retry-After header, sleep that long then continue with backoff counter reset or increment? I prefer reset to avoid huge waits.
Sam: also note transient 5xx should increment the retry count. For 429 we should prioritize honoring Retry-After first. If Retry-After > max_backoff, treat as strong signal to fail fast or route to a lower-tier model.
Joel: language quirks: Python SDK exposes retry config as RetryConfig(initial_ms, max_ms, multiplier, max_attempts, jitter='full'). Node exposes similar but with middleware hook. Rust client (experimental) avoids blocking sleeps — uses async sleep and caps total retry budget per request.
Alex: streaming-specific: any resume token support?
Priya: currently only supported for embeddings & a few structured read endpoints. For chat/streaming completions we don't have resume tokens — plan to add in future. If you need resumability, do non-streaming or implement server-side chunk checkpointing.
Sam: quick note on idempotency keys: choose a key per logical user action, not per HTTP call. If the client auto-generates per attempt you'll break dedupe. Recommend SDK auto-generate but return key to caller so app can supply its own stable key when needed.
Alex: got it. I'll open a small PR to Node SDK to add Retry-After handling + example for stream fallback.
Joel: please add integration test that simulates 429 with Retry-After and verifies SDK waits then retries.
DevEx Bot: FYI docs: https://redwood.example.devex/retries — includes code samples and recommended defaults.
Priya: thanks all :thumbsup: if you need I can post the exact code snippet for jitter formula (full jitter = random(0, base * 2^attempt)).
Alex: that would be great, thanks Priya. I'll tag you on the PR.
Sam: ping me for the canary run after the PR — we'll run dedicated capacity test to ensure no regression.
Alex: noted, will do.
